name.la: De ascensione mentis in Deum per scalas rerum creatarum
name.en-US: The Mind's Ascent to God by the Ladder of Created Things
name.pt-BR: A ascensão da mente a Deus pela escada das criaturas

description.la: Quindecim gradus ex creaturarum consideratione ad Deum ascendentium (1615), opus ascetica ex anno recessus conscriptum. Textus ex editione Vivès (1870-74), ex scanno OCR.
description.en-US: Fifteen steps of ascent to God through the consideration of creatures, written on Bellarmine's annual retreat (1615). The Latin is the Vivès edition (1870-74) from an OCR scan; the English is the 1925 translation by a Religious of the Church of England (A. R. Mowbray).
description.pt-BR: Quinze degraus de ascensão a Deus pela consideração das criaturas, escritos no retiro anual do cardeal (1615).

en-US.translator: A Religious of the Church of England ("Monialis")

sources.edition: Roberti Bellarmini Opera omnia, ed. Justin Fèvre, tom. 8 (Paris: Vivès, 1870-74).
sources.description: Archive.org OCR (djvu.txt, Boston College copy) cleaned by script: running heads, page numbers and the reference-only footnote blocks removed, line-end hyphens joined, recognisable OCR slips corrected by a lexicon pass, so some remain.
sources.tierEvidence: Bellarmine died in 1621; the Vivès edition of 1870-74 is public domain.

sources.edition: The Mind's Ascent to God, trans. a Religious of the Church of England (Monialis), with a preface by P. N. Waggett (London: A. R. Mowbray, 1925).
sources.description: Archive.org OCR (djvu.txt), paragraphs rejoined and page heads removed; the steps hold the translator's chapters as ## headings; the translator's division of the Latin into chapters is kept inside each step. Some chapter-opening letters lost to the drop-cap are not restored.
sources.tierEvidence: Published 1925 in Great Britain; the translator was anonymous and the book is public domain in the US.
